newsitem.title: USA: Lock problems halt barge traffic on Illinois River.
newsitem.headline: Lock problems halt barge traffic on Illinois River.

text.p: The LaGrange lock on the Illinois River which has been closed since Wednesday is expected to be reopened Thursday, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers officials said.
The lock, near Beardstown, Ill., was shut down by a mechanical failure and has halted barge traffic north and south of the lock since Wednesday, officials said.
"There are 18 tows sitting here now with 216 barges. They cannot get through," LaGrange lockmaster Stan Wallace said Thursday.
Mike Zerbonia, chief of maintenance with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, told Reuters the lock should be reopened later Thursday at about 1430 to 1500 CST.
"The divers repaired the hydraulic leak and right now they're cleaning up the oil spill," Zerbonia said.
Much of Illinois was hit by snowfall and bitter cold temperatures on Thursday.

"We have divers in the water trying to locate the leak. The cold weather and snow in west central Illinois is not helping us because it limits the amount of time divers can take in the water to repair the leak," Wallace said.
"They can only spend about 20 minutes a time in the water," Wallace said. He noted that it started snowing last night and his area already had four to five inches of snow.
Cold weather has not hampered barge traffic in other parts of the Illinois River, he said.
"The channel is open. We have two inches of running ice but it is breaking up and barge traffic is able to move," Zerbonia said of areas other than the LaGrange lock.
"I have not heard of any problems from Hannibal, Mo., down to the mouth of the Ohio River, said Ken Kruchowski, spokesman with the U.S. Army Corps of engineers, St Louis district.
He added there were repairs scheduled at Lock and Dam 24, at Clarksville, Mo. until about February 1.

"That has closed Lock and Dam 24 during the daytime hours from 6.00 AM to 6.00 PM CST," Kruchowski said. "Lock and Dam 25, near Winfield, Mo., is (also) having repair work done but that has not affected barge traffic."
"There are ice floes on the upper Mississippi but traffic has not been hampered at this point," he said.
But ice jams on the river system may become a factor in the future depending how long and how cold it gets.
"The thing that will affect traffic is the cold weather because of the ice," Kruchowski said.

Ron Fournier, chief of public affairs, U.S. Army Corps of Enginner, Rock Island District, Ill., said the navigation industry has basically stopped shipping in the middle of December from Lock and Dam 19, at Keokuk, Iowa, to Minneapolis. "They do this in expectation for poor shipping conditions during the winter months," Fournier said.
